# ValuePreview

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:value-preview` · Kerf UI · component · Structure

A bounded, read-only multiline text value with keyboard scrolling.

## When to use

Display a literal long value with line breaks and long tokens inside a bounded scroll region.

- A read-only value may have multiple lines or long unbroken text and needs bounded scrolling, such as a conflict version.

**Not when:**

- Do not use for editing; use a multiline TextField.
- Do not use for short label/value facts; use ValueTable.

**Alternatives:**

- [ValueTable](./value-table.md) (nearest) — Use ValueTable for rows of short labelled facts.

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/value-preview` — exports `ValuePreview`.
- CSS: the browser build of `@kerfjs/ui/value-preview` pulls its CSS automatically; import `@kerfjs/ui/value-preview.css` manually only without the `browser` export condition.
- Declared side effects: browser-condition-css.

## Geometry

Margin: none · border: none · padding: none (layout role: structure). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

## Accessibility

- Give the focusable output a label so keyboard and screen-reader users can identify and scroll it.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Public class hooks (select for layout placement only, never to change the component's look): `kui-value-preview`.

Never put `kui-value-preview` on an element you write; render `ValuePreview` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Public tokens it reads: `--kui-color-text`, `--kui-font-xs`, `--kui-focus-ring`. Set a token only where its public contract allows; prefer a prop.

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
